Suppress specific warnings by message and stack

Source: R/suppress_warnings.R
suppress_warnings_from.Rd

Runs an expression and suppresses only warnings that match all supplied criteria. Criteria may include warning text and whether the trimmed warning stack contains a package/environment name or function name.

suppress_warnings_from(
  expr,
  message = NULL,
  fun = NULL,
  package = NULL,
  fixed = TRUE
)

Arguments

expr

Expression to evaluate.

message

Optional character pattern matched against conditionMessage(). If NULL, the warning message is not checked.

fun

Optional function name that must appear in the trimmed warning stack. If NULL, the stack function name is not checked.

package

Optional package or environment name that must appear in the trimmed warning stack, for example "Matrix" or "R_GlobalEnv". If NULL, the stack package/environment is not checked.

fixed

Logical scalar passed to grepl(). Use TRUE for literal message matching and FALSE for regular expressions.

Value

The value of expr, with matching warnings suppressed.

Details

The stack is trimmed at the warning's conditionCall() before matching. If all filters are NULL, this suppresses all warnings from expr.

If both fun and package arguments are supplied, they must match at the same frame of the stack.

Examples

f <- function() {
  warning("f warned")
}

suppress_warnings_from(
  f(),
  message = "f warned",
  package = "R_GlobalEnv",
  fun = "f"
)
#> Warning: f warned
